info.name: Hugo
info.description:
Every Hugo REST route, plus MCP and A2A JSON-RPC examples, organized by area. Hugo is a multi-tenant super agent server: you give it access to the systems behind your production stack, group that access into agent profiles, and reach those profiles over MCP, A2A, REST, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or the dashboard. The full reference is REST_API.md, MCP_API.md, and A2A_API.md in the repository.

How to use it

1. Import this collection and `Hugo.postman_environment.json`, and select the environment.
2. Set `host` and `port` for your server. The Docker stack serves the API on 127.0.0.1:8800; the seeded demo stack in `docker/factory/` serves it on 127.0.0.1:8810.
3. Set `password` and `adminPassword` to the accounts' passwords (`password` on a fresh stack). The collection never changes them: since D-048 `mustChangePassword` is advisory and blocks nothing. If you changed the seeded passwords to one value, you can leave `password` alone and put that value in `newPassword`; the collection tries it when `password` is refused. Against the factory demo stack, set both to that stack's demo password.
4. Run the folders in order (Collection Runner or `scripts/newman.sh`). Later folders use IDs that earlier folders capture into collection variables.

Authentication

The collection uses a bearer token. Its pre-request script keeps `{{token}}` (the tenant administrator `{{email}}`) and `{{adminToken}}` (the system administrator `{{adminEmail}}`) valid and only calls the server when a token is missing or about to expire. Requests that show another scheme (credential keys, a signed request, anonymous routes) set their own authorization. Token routes are rate limited to 10 per minute per IP by default (`Auth.RateLimitPerMinute`); the run stays under that, and the sign-in script waits out a 429 (honoring `Retry-After`) and tries once more.

Credentials do not inherit their owner's administrator bypass, so every credential the collection creates gets an explicit role (`roleName`).

What runs where

Everything runs against a fresh server with nothing else installed: the examples use `demo-db`, a SQLite resource on `:memory:`. Requests that need a model (chat, A2A tasks, the OpenAI-compatible completions, `ask_agent_smith`) are skipped unless `modelBaseUrl` is set to a reachable OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Requests that would restart the server or hold a stream open forever are documented but always skipped. The last folder deletes what the run created.

exec: // Collection pre-request script: keeps {{token}} (the tenant administrator, {{email}}) and {{adminToken}}
// (the system administrator, {{adminEmail}}) valid. It runs before every request but only calls the server when a
// token is missing or expires within a minute. Sign-in tries {{password}} (or {{adminPassword}}) first and, when that
// is refused and {{newPassword}} is set, {{newPassword}}, for servers whose seeded passwords were already changed.
// The password that worked is kept in {{currentPassword}} (or {{adminCurrentPassword}}) for the requests that need
// it. Nothing changes a password here: mustChangePassword is advisory (D-048) and blocks no route.
// Token routes are rate limited (Auth.RateLimitPerMinute, default 10 per minute per IP); a 429 is retried once after
setTimeout(function () { signIn(email, password, callback, true); }, wait);
if (body) { store(prefix, body, primary); done(); return; }
if (second) { store(prefix, second, alternate); done(); return; }
console.warn('Hugo: could not sign in as ' + email);

item.name: Health and server info
item.description: Anonymous and lightly authenticated routes that tell you whether Hugo is up and what it is. Point load balancers and container healthchecks at `/v1.0/api/health/live` (process is running) or `/v1.0/api/health` (database answers, schema current, not draining). The OpenAPI document at `/openapi.json` is generated from the same route registrations this collection exercises.

request.description: Readiness check. Returns 200 with `status: healthy` when the database answers, the schema version matches the binary, and the server is not draining; 503 otherwise. No authentication.
Same check as `/v1.0/api/health`, under the conventional readiness path.
Liveness: 200 for as long as the process runs, even when the database is unreachable. Use it for restart decisions, not for routing.
Prometheus exposition text relayed from the metrics listener. Returns 404 when `Telemetry.ServeMetricsOnServicePort` is false. No authentication: keep the port on a private network.
The generated OpenAPI 3 document for every route. No authentication.
Swagger UI over `/openapi.json` (HTML). No authentication.
Product version, node ID, the public REST, MCP, and A2A URLs, the database type, feature flags, and the observability endpoints. Any authenticated principal may call it.
Alias of `/v1.0/api/server-info`.
Reachability of the configured observability services (Prometheus, Grafana, Tempo, Loki). Results are cached for 30 seconds. Needs Read on Settings.

item.name: Tokens and sign-in
item.description:
Session tokens are how people and most automation talk to Hugo. `POST /v1.0/token` accepts either user login headers (`x-email`, `x-password`, `x-tenant-id`) or credential keys (`x-access-key`, `x-secret-key`) and returns an opaque bearer token. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (or `x-token`). The collection's pre-request script already keeps `{{token}}` and `{{adminToken}}` fresh; the requests here show each token route on its own.

Token routes are rate limited per source IP and per identity (`Auth.RateLimitPerMinute`, default 10 per minute) and answer 429 with `Retry-After: 60` when exceeded.

request.description: Tenant discovery for login forms: the tenants an email can sign in to. Anonymous and rate limited. Returns an empty array for unknown emails, so it does not confirm whether an account exists elsewhere.

item.name: Agent profiles and bindings
item.description:
An agent profile is what a caller talks to: a persona, instructions, model endpoints, exposure flags for MCP, A2A, and the OpenAI-compatible surface, and a set of bindings. A binding attaches a resource to a profile under an alias with an access mode (`ReadOnly`, `ReadWriteWithApproval`, `ReadWrite`), tool rules, deny patterns, and an optional instruction override. Every tenant starts with the `Hugo` profile (persona Agent Smith, who calls you Mr. Anderson).

This folder runs before the resource folder needs it: it creates the `demo-db` resource (an in-memory SQLite database that works on any server) and binds it to `Hugo` and to a second profile, `Oncall`, where writes need approval.

item.name: Connectors and resources
item.description: Connectors are the code that knows a service family; resources are your configured instances of them. `GET /v1.0/api/connectors` describes every connector: its settings schema (what a resource form needs), its secret slots, and its tools with their effect classification. Resources reference secrets by slot and never hold credential values themselves. Test a configuration before saving it with `POST /v1.0/api/resources/test`.

request.description: Every loaded connector with settings schema, secret slots, and tools. Needs Read on Connector.
One connector descriptor by type.

Validate and test a resource configuration without storing it. Validation problems come back in `validationErrors`; a failed connection is still a 200 with `success: false`. The test is cancelled after `Connectors.TestTimeoutSeconds`.

Test a saved resource's connection and record the result in `lastTestUtc`, `lastTestResult`, and `lastTestMessage`. SSH resources pin the host key on first success (trust on first use).

`POST /v1.0/api/tool-invocations/dry-run` runs everything in the invocation pipeline except the tool itself: profile and binding resolution, authorization, argument validation against the tool schema, effect classification, tool rules, deny patterns, and the access-mode decision. Nothing is executed or recorded, so none of these requests needs the target system to exist.

The folder creates one placeholder resource per connector family, binds each to the `Oncall` profile (ReadWriteWithApproval), and asks Hugo what it would decide for a representative call. The cleanup folder deletes the placeholders.

item.name: MCP
item.description:
Hugo serves MCP (Streamable HTTP) at `/mcp` and `/mcp/{profileName}` on the REST port. Authenticate with the REST schemes. The profile comes from the path, the `x-hugo-profile` header, the credential's bound profile, the user's default profile, or the tenant default, in that order (D-018).

With protocol revisions up to 2025-11-25, start with `initialize` and send the returned `Mcp-Session-Id` on every later request. Sessions live in memory: after a server restart the old session ID gets 404 and the client initializes again. Responses may arrive as JSON or as an SSE stream; long tool calls stream keep-alives. See MCP_API.md for every tool.
